top_problem: The baseline grid is broken where it matters: La Botella and El Barril sit 2 pt off the 6 pt grid that El Cantarito and La Rosa use, so right-column rows never line up with left-column rows. Also, the boldest missing idea: the cards do not read as real lotería cards. They have no numbered corners, no portrait tabla proportion, and the featured card is a giant generic jug that pushes the highest-margin drinks into the bottom third.
fixes: Resize the right cards to 6 pt multiples that still add up to 594 pt (for example 192 / 210 / 192 with 12 pt gaps), so every subhead and item row on all four cards lands on the same 12 pt grid from the 138 pt deck top, and cross_card_baseline_alignment comes back true.

Cut El Cantarito's face from 394 pt to about 240-260 pt (on-grid) and give the space back to the cocktail list with larger item type or a signature pick, because cocktails are the highest-margin section and now start 420 pt down the page.
Use one description treatment on every card, either all stacked under the name or all inline, and give the spirits a type or age line so La Botella is not a bare price list.

Make the featured card's subhead space above 12.0 pt instead of 12.75 pt, and use the same cartouche height on every card (or a declared 1.5x step on the grid), so header spacing is identical across columns.

Push the lotería idea further with printed card numbers in the corners, portrait tabla proportions and a lotería-style bold figure frame, so the deck reads as a real tabla and not four coloured boxes with icons.

top_problem: The card-title level uses two styles. EL CANTARITO sits in a 36 pt name bar at a visibly larger cap size with a 10 pt gloss. LA BOTELLA, EL BARRIL and LA ROSA use 24 pt bars with 12 pt caps and an 8.5 pt gloss. The proposal says there is 'one size on every card', but the render contradicts it, which is an automatic fail on criterion 2. There are other problems too. The measured cross_card_baseline_alignment is False: the La Botella and El Barril subheads and item rows sit 2.0 pt and 1.99 pt off the 6 pt grid, so the two columns do not share rows. Space above the second subhead is 12.75 pt on Cantarito but 12.0 pt on the other cards (subhead_space_above_is_12pt = False). Titles are centred on their bars while subheads are ranged left. On the right cards the verse is centred in the space beside the figure rather than on the card, so the face and the name bar have different centre axes. Seven subheads for 14 items leave three single-item subsections (Brandy, Cider, Sparkling), and these clutter the hierarchy. Boldest missing idea: the name bars read as generic coloured banners, not lotería cartouches. The header system should be the classic lotería card: a numbered, boxed serif name under the figure, at one size, turning each section title into a real card you could call out.
fixes: Set every card title to one size and one bar height (same caps size, tracking and gloss size), and signal the featured card only by its taller face.

Put the right-column deck on the same grid as the left: take up the 2 pt offset on La Botella and El Barril (for example, adjust the 12 pt card gaps or the face height) so subheads and item rows line up across the gutter.
Make the space above subheads exactly 12 pt on El Cantarito, like the other cards, and increase the name-bar-to-first-subhead gap from 6 pt to 12 pt so a subhead does not crowd the bar above it.

Put all header elements on one axis: either range the card titles and glosses left at the 324/48 pt item edge, or centre the subheads (and centre the right-card verses on the card, not beside the figure).
Merge the single-item subsections (drop Brandy, Cider and Sparkling as subheads, or fold each item into its neighbour group with a small inline label) so each subhead heads at least two items.

top_problem: The palette is a correct lotería set of four hues plus cream and ink, but it is applied as colour-coding and not as a system. Ink/black La Botella reads as a default card beside three saturated ones. Marigold, the warmest hue, never touches the type. Prices are bare numerals the same size and weight as the names, so the menu has no signature number treatment. The boldest missing idea: the numbers as lotería card numerals, where each card's prices and its numbered card corner become the graphic system, instead of a cantarito illustration that pushes the high-margin cocktails into the bottom third of the page.
fixes: Give La Botella a true palette hue (for example a deep agave-blue or mezcal smoke) or a marigold name bar with ink text, so four saturated cards read as one deck instead of three colours and a black default.

Give the prices a signature treatment, for example Fraunces 700 at 11.5 to 12 pt with real tabular lining figures (tnum), optionally in a small lotería-number roundel or with a dotted leader in the card colour, so the numbers stand out without shouting and '11' no longer sits narrower than its neighbours.

Shrink the cantarito face on the featured card to about 45 percent of the column and use the space it frees to lift the cocktails, the highest-margin section, into the upper half of the page with room for more signature serves.

Bring marigold into the type system as one controlled accent (for example the '&' in the title, the subhead rules or the featured-card prices on the terracotta ground), so the fourth colour works as more than decoration in the flags.
Snap cards 2 and 3 onto the 6 pt grid (they are 2 pt off) so that item rows line up across the gutter with El Cantarito.

Use a grid of true-proportion numbered cards, each drink category a card with its own number, bold figure and caller verse, and give the cocktails a card each, so the deck itself is the menu and not trim on top of a list.
fixes: Shrink the El Cantarito face to at most 40% of the card, or give each of the four cocktails its own small lotería card, so the cocktails move up into the prime upper-left spot and the empty tan panel goes away.

Bring back the core lotería signifiers: card numbers in the corner, the classic tall card ratio with a thick border, and the name set in the traditional bottom band. Right now the concept reads as generic framed boxes.

Build all four faces the same way. The featured card has the verse centred above the figure while the right cards have a small figure at left and the verse at right. Pick one composition and scale it.
Snap La Botella and El Barril to the shared 6/12 pt grid (they are 2 pt off), make subhead space above exactly 12 pt on El Cantarito, and set the cartouche at one size or a clear 2:1 ratio.

Make the descriptions consistent. Either stack all descriptions under the name like the cocktails, or put them all inline. Give the spirits a one-line note so the La Botella card is not a bare price list next to described items.

lens: every item and price vs the draft (build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: All 14 draft items are present, none are invented, and all 14 prices match the draft exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Old Fashioned 16, Daiquiri 14, Blanco 12, Añejo 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Pilsner 7, IPA 8, Amber 7, Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13). The problem is descriptions. The three spirits (Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP) now print no description at all: their desc is "" in round-10/doc.json, although the draft had 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.'. The beer, cider and wine lines use generic category wording ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') with no ABV, grape or region, so the reverse of the La Botella, El Barril and La Rosa cards reads as a bare price list next to a fully described cocktail card. Everything missing is flagged in missing_ingredients, so this is not an automatic fail, but the guest-facing content is thin. Content average 71.4, below the 80 needed.
fixes: Put back a description for Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP using only known facts (for example 'Unaged blanco tequila.', 'Barrel-aged añejo tequila.', 'VSOP Cognac.') so every item has a description line, and keep the brand, pour size and age statement flags open for the venue.

Replace the category wording in the beer, cider and wine descriptions with guest language drawn from known facts, and add a visible placeholder slot for ABV (beer and cider) and region (wine) so the missing facts are asked for; do not print category labels as descriptions.
Use one description style across all four cards: cocktails put the description on a second line, while beer, cider and wine run it inline after the name; pick one and apply it everywhere.

Use one price style across all four cards: Spirits prices are black while every other card uses its accent colour; make them match (all accent or all neutral), and resolve the unlabelled Brut Rosé price (glass or bottle) with the venue before print.

Rebalance the page so the Cantarito figure face does not take about half the cocktail card while the Spirits card has no descriptions; give the space back to content (for example the agave spirits' descriptions) so every category carries similar editorial weight.

top_problem: The menu has three different description levels. The 4 cocktails get full spirit, modifier and garnish lines. Beer, cider and wine get 3-word draft fragments ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') with no ABV, region or producer. The 3 spirits have no description at all: the draft lines 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.' were removed. So 10 of 14 items fail criterion 8's ingredient standard. They are flagged, which avoids an automatic fail, but on paper the menu reads as half-finished. Prices: all 14 match build/draft_doc.json exactly, and nothing was invented or left off. Section order changed from the draft's cocktails, beer, wine, spirits, cider to cocktails, spirits, beer & cider, wine.
fixes: Give each spirit a guest line instead of printing its name alone. Use a type/age line from the rows already cited (for example Cognac VSOP: 'grape brandy', from path a88f6e79) and flag brand, age and pour. Until then, keep the draft words rather than a blank, because the scorecard's measured check needs a description element for every item.

Stop spending about 60% of El Cantarito's face on the jug figure while the four cocktails, the highest-margin items, are packed into the bottom of the page. Cut the face height so the cocktail list starts in the upper half of the left column, which is the prime spot.

Set all descriptions in one style. Right now cocktails are stacked on their own lines, beer and wine sit inline on the name line, and spirits have nothing. Pick one treatment, and push the Coordinator to get ABV for the 3 beers and the cider and a region for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé, so every category reaches the same completeness.

Label Brut Rosé as glass or bottle, or add a visible 'price label pending' note in the proof. Putting it under a separate Sparkling subhead does not remove the unlabelled-price problem for criterion 3.

Make proposal.md match the printed menu. It says Brut Rosé sits under 'Espumoso', apart from a 'Por copa' list, but the render prints 'Sparkling' and 'By the Glass' (the page itself is consistent English-only). Also confirm that the garnish and glass facts (lime wheel, coupe, orange peel, lime coin) come from the phg.recipe_versions rows, because none of them is in the draft's components.

Beer and cider show no ABV and wine shows no region; all flagged, but the printed lines are 3 words each and fall far short of criterion 8.
Section order moved away from the draft (spirits now come before beer and wine); this can be defended with an agave-first cantina argument, but proposal.md never states the reason.
The cocktail list, the best sellers, sits below a very large illustration; the other categories get small faces, so categories are not treated equally.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The flow puts content second. The cocktail card is the highest-margin category and the lead of the menu, yet the cantarito illustration takes the top 60% of the left column, so all four cocktails sit below the fold in the bottom-left corner. The prime top-left spot holds no items. On the right, the agave spirits run as a bare list of names while beer and wine get descriptions, so the categories are not treated equally. Mezcal or agave depth could anchor a cantina, but the draft has none.
problems: Section order Cocktails > Spirits (agave) > Beer & Cider > Wine suits a cantina, and all 14 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json with nothing invented or dropped. But the reading path makes guests pass a full-height illustration before they reach any cocktail.

La Botella (Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP) is printed with names only. It is the only card with no description line, which breaks equal treatment and the spirits rule (type/age). It is flagged, but the card reads as unfinished at the second-most-important spot for an agave-led venue.

Beer lines have no ABV, and 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' mostly repeats the name. Wine lines give no region ('Dry red wine.'). All are flagged in needs_input, but they sit short of the criterion-8 standard.
Brut Rosé 13 sits under Sparkling, right below the By the Glass list, with no glass/bottle label, so guests will read it as a glass price. The source label is empty, so this is ambiguous.
A one-item Brandy subheader (Cognac VSOP) and a one-item Cider subheader make thin sections that fragment the right column.

Price format is consistent (whole numbers, no $), but the placement differs: cocktails put the price on the name line above a wrapped description, while other cards set the description inline between name and price. Price colour also changes per card.
proposal.md refers to 'Espumoso' and 'Por copa' subheaders, but the print shows English 'Sparkling' and 'By the Glass'. The documentation does not match the artwork (coherence).
fixes: Shrink the El Cantarito face to about 35% of the card height and raise the cocktail list, so the Margarita and the House Originals land in the top-left prime zone.

Give each spirit a sourced type/age line (for example 'Blanco / plata tequila', 'Añejo tequila', 'Cognac, VSOP'), or print pour size once supplied, so La Botella matches the other cards; keep brand and age flagged until the venue answers.
Add a label ('glass' or 'bottle') to the Brut Rosé price once the venue confirms. Until then, move Sparkling out from under By the Glass or set the price with a visible pending marker.
Merge the single-item subheads: set Cognac under an 'Agave & Brandy' or plain spirits list, and fold Dry Cider into the beer list with a style tag. This removes the thin one-line sections.
Get ABV for the beers and region for the wines through the Coordinator, and replace 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' with a line that does not repeat the item name.

top_problem: The menu is written in three different voices. Cocktails get full guest sentences with italic serve cues. Beer, cider and wine get three-word category lines on the name row ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). Spirits get no description at all. Add in the untranslated Spanish verses on top of English-only subheaders, and the copy reads like three menus sharing one frame. Measured against the draft, every price and item is present and exact (14 of 14, nothing added or dropped).
fixes: Write one guest line for each spirit using only known facts: type and age come from the names and the cited beverage_categories rows (for example 'Aged tequila, sipped neat' only if the pour is confirmed; otherwise use 'Tequila añejo' plus a style word from the row). Keep brand and pour flagged. Name-only items fail the 'every item has a description' requirement in criterion 8.

Put all four cards in one description voice and one layout. Either give beer, wine and cider the same stacked line under the name as the cocktails, with style and ABV for beer and grape and region for wine left as visible TBC flags until the venue supplies them, or move the cocktails inline. Do not mix inline taxonomy fragments with stacked sentences.
Label Brut Rosé as glass or bottle before print (the draft label is empty). Right now it sits under Sparkling right after the By the Glass list, so a guest will read $13 as a glass price.

Rebalance the cocktail card and section flow. The jug figure takes roughly 60% of the only card with real copy, and the high-margin House Originals sit under the Classics. Put House Originals first or give them equal prime space, and consider the scorecard order: cocktails, then beer, then wine, then spirits (or state why an agave-first spirits card beats it for this venue).

Make the verses and the proposal agree with the printed menu. Add a small English gloss to each Spanish verse (or drop the two drinking-joke verses, per open flag 7). Fix proposal.md, which still says 'Espumoso' and 'Por copa' when the print says 'Sparkling' and 'By the Glass'.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged
top_problem: The missing data is flagged well behind the scenes (14 missing_ingredients flags in doc.json and 7 needs_input questions in proposal.md), but the printed menu handles it by leaving things out. Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP print as bare names, even though the draft gave each one a line ('Blanco tequila pour.' etc.), so the scorecard's own check that every item has a description fails for 3 of 14 items. Beer prints with no ABV and wine with no region, and nothing on the page tells the guest a detail is still to come. The Brut Rosé $13 prints with no glass or bottle label, so a guest could read it either way. On the page, the gaps look like finished content instead of open questions. Separately, the Manhattan line leaves out the draft's 'aromatic bitters' while the Old Fashioned prints 'bitters', so the same ingredient is treated two ways. All 14 prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly, with no items invented or dropped (the retired Junmai Ginjo is noted and left off).
fixes: Give each spirit a one-line type descriptor built from the draft words and the cited beverage_categories rows (e.g. 'Blanco tequila' / 'Añejo tequila' / 'VSOP Cognac, grape brandy'), set on the name line like the beer, so no item prints without a description while brand, age and pour stay flagged.

Hold the Brut Rosé price, or its Sparkling line, out of the print release until the venue answers glass or bottle, and make this a blocking needs_input item, because an unlabelled $13 sparkling price will be misread by guests and staff.

Add one consistent pour-size note for beer, wine and spirits (e.g. under each subheader) as soon as the venue answers, and until then mark those sub-sections pending-data in doc.json so the proposal cannot be treated as publishable.

Make the Manhattan and Old Fashioned handle bitters the same way: either restore the draft's 'aromatic bitters' in the Manhattan line or remove 'bitters' from the Old Fashioned until public_components is confirmed. Also cite the recipe_versions row id for every printed garnish and glass ('lime wheel', 'lime coin', 'coupe', 'orange peel'), since the source table currently lists 'none'.

Bring the three content voices closer together (full cocktail sentences, three-word beer/wine lines, blank spirits) by giving wine at least the grape and style ('Malbec, dry red') and beer its style from the draft, and remove the stale 'Espumoso' and 'Por copa' references from proposal.md and doc.json now that the subheaders are English only.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass and serve to sources
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source. But outside the four cocktails the copy is either blank or taxonomy. The three spirits have no line, Malbec and Pinot Grigio say only 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.', and 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' mostly repeats the item name. The Manhattan also drops the aromatic bitters that the venue's own draft description and recipe print (menu_items 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.'; draft_doc Manhattan component 'Aromatic Bitters'), while the Old Fashioned prints 'bitters'.

'blanco tequila, fresh lime, orange liqueur and agave syrup' matches draft_doc components Tequila Blanco / Fresh Lime Juice / Orange Liqueur / Agave Syrup (prep). 'Bright and citrus-forward' is from menu_items.menu_description.
Manhattan 'In a coupe, cocktail cherry': recipe_versions 9fb77eaa glassware 'Coupe', garnish 'Cocktail cherry'. 'Rye whiskey' matches draft_doc component 'Rye Whiskey'.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'Over one large cube, orange peel': recipe_versions 7095fd3d method 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube', garnish 'Orange peel'. 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara and bitters' matches menu_items description and draft_doc components.

House Daiquiri 'In a coupe, lime coin': recipe_versions 14d45e57 glassware 'Coupe', garnish 'Lime coin'. 'house demerara syrup' matches menu_items description and draft_doc prep 'Demerara Syrup' ('House 1:1 demerara syrup by weight').

Beer, cider and wine lines match menu_items.menu_description verbatim (gateway log_id 158). Spirits are name-only, so no fact there needs a source. Spanish verses are spelled correctly (cántaro, albañil, quedó) and are cultural text, not item facts.
problems: Crit 12: the spirits card has no guest language at all, and the wine and beer lines read like category labels ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). The cocktail lines have one voice, but it is a spec list plus a serve cue, not appetising prose.

Crit 11: Manhattan omits the aromatic bitters that are in the venue's own description and recipe. That is less faithful to the source than the draft, and it is inconsistent with the Old Fashioned printing 'bitters'.

Crit 14: Brut Rosé 13 has no glass or bottle label (the draft label is empty). No pour sizes appear on spirits, beer or wine. The Daiquiri's serve cue breaks to a two-word last line ('lime coin.') at print size.

Crit 13: the lotería deck and the Spanish are a strong cultural fit. But the masthead is the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' with no venue name. The agave list is only two tequilas with no brand or mezcal, which is thin for a cantina. Nothing is local to Iowa City (no brewery named), and two verses joke about drunkenness, which is risky for a college-town bar.

Crit 10: proposal.md contradicts the render. It says Brut Rosé sits under an 'Espumoso' subheader apart from the 'Por copa' list, but the menu prints 'SPARKLING' and 'BY THE GLASS' (layout.json subheaders).
fixes: Restore 'aromatic bitters' to the Manhattan line (menu_items description; draft_doc component 'Aromatic Bitters'), or get written venue confirmation to hide it and make the Old Fashioned consistent.

Ask the venue for producer, region and ABV for the wines and beers, and brand, age and pour size for the spirits. Until they arrive, write sourced guest lines, e.g. use the Margarita-style flavour note where the draft has one, rather than bare category words.
Label Brut Rosé as glass or bottle as soon as the venue answers. Until then keep the flag and do not print it as a by-the-glass price.
Put the venue's real name on the masthead, and have the venue decide on the two drinking-joke verses before print.
Correct proposal.md so the subheader names ('By the Glass', 'Sparkling') match the rendered menu.

Ask the venue to swap or drop the two drunkenness verses and to add the agave depth a cantina guest expects (mezcal, a second agave cocktail, Mexican beer). This is a content request; do not invent any of it.

problems: Coherence (10): proposal.md says Brut Rosé sits under an 'Espumoso' subheader, apart from a 'Por copa' list. The render and layout.json print 'SPARKLING' and 'BY THE GLASS'. The proposal and the files disagree.

Quality (12): the wine, beer and cider lines are category labels or restate the name ('Brut' already means dry; 'Dry Cider' / 'Dry sparkling cider'). The spirits have no line at all. There are three voices across four cards.

Venue fit (13): the loteria system, correct Spanish and cantina card names are strong and ownable. But agave depth is two unnamed tequilas with no mezcal. Only 1 of 4 cocktails is agave-based, and the 'House Originals' (a brown butter Old Fashioned and a Daiquiri) do not read as cantina. The printed page shows nothing specific to Iowa City beyond the location line. The $14-16 cocktails are the top tier for a ZIP with a $52,960 median income and a median age of 28.6. That is defensible for a downtown cocktail bar, but nothing on the page (such as a pour size or brand) justifies the price.

Layout (14): the spirit prices have no pour label (what does $12 buy?). Brut Rosé's $13 is ambiguous between glass and bottle. The italic serve cues break mid-phrase ('Over / one large cube, orange peel.'; 'In a coupe, / lime coin.'), so the cue falls onto its own line and looks orphaned. The beer and wine inline fragments are tidy, but they are so short that the right side of each card is empty ragged space next to the prices.
fixes: Get pour size, brand and age for the three spirits and print one guest line per spirit, plus a pour label in the Agave/Brandy subhead (for example 'AGAVE · 2 oz'), so La Botella carries the cantina's core category; until then flag it as missing_ingredients.
Put 'aromatic bitters' back in the Manhattan line (menu_items bf732e78 menu_description) unless the venue confirms in writing that it should be hidden.

Ask the venue for producer, region, style and ABV for the 7 beer/cider/wine items so each line becomes an appetising guest line in the cocktail voice, not a restated category; at minimum, remove 'draft' from the IPA line under the DRAFT subhead.

Designer layout note: keep each italic serve cue unbroken (use a non-breaking space inside 'one large cube' and 'lime coin', or tighten the measure) so no serve cue splits across lines at print or phone size.

problems: Criterion 14: 'By the Glass' wines, the Brut Rosé and all three spirits show prices with no pour, glass or bottle label. The Brut Rosé's missing label is an open needs_input item, but it is printed anyway.

Criterion 14: the inline beer and wine tags (about 9 pt, muted) sit 40-60% of the measure away from right-aligned prices with no leader. Stacked cocktail descriptions against inline tags against bare spirit names means three layouts for one element type.

Criterion 12: the beer, cider and wine lines are class labels or restate the name: 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', 'Dry sparkling cider.', 'Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'. That is database-class wording on 7 of 14 items. The cocktail lines are good guest copy.

Pick one description system for the whole deck: a name/price line with the description beneath at one measure, or a consistent inline treatment with a dotted leader to the price. Apply it to beer, wine and cocktails alike.
Keep the serve cues from breaking mid-phrase: keep 'over one large cube' and 'in a coupe, lime coin' together with non-breaking spaces, or shorten the character clause so each cue fits on one line.

Replace the class-label beer and wine tags with sourced guest language, or drop to name-only like the spirits, until the venue supplies brewery, producer, region and ABV. Do not print lines that only restate the item name.

Restore 'aromatic bitters' to the Manhattan line to match the draft menu_description (menu_items bf732e78). Sync proposal.md subheader names with the render and export real x/y/w geometry for the item_name, description and price elements.
